title: Tahini Apple Galette with Cardamom
changes_from_base: A cardamom apple galette over a sweet tahini spread with a sesame crust, in place of a crème pâtissière fruit tart.
summary: A flaky apple galette spiced with cardamom, baked over a sweet tahini spread and finished with sesame seeds.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
cold unsalted butter, in small cubes
fine sea salt or table salt
crisp, tart apples such as Pink Lady (about 6)

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: whisk the flour, sugar and salt in the large bowl. Toss in the butter, then flatten each cube once between your fingers. Flattened butter pieces make long flaky layers.

steps.title: Water
steps.text: drizzle 60 ml iced water over and keep raking it through with your fingers until shaggy. Knead briefly into a ball with no dry patches, adding up to 2 tbsp more water if needed. Wrap as a 2.5 cm thick disc and chill 2 h (or up to 3 days).

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: on a floured surface roll to a 35 cm round and lift it onto the paper-lined tray. Keep it in the fridge while you make the rest.

steps.title: Sesame spread
steps.text: whisk the tahini, sugar, soft butter, egg and salt until smooth.

steps.title: Apples
steps.text: heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) with a shelf low down. Peel, core and thinly slice the apples, then toss with the lemon juice, 40 g of the sugar and the cardamom until the sugar dissolves.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: spread the tahini mix over the pastry, leaving 5 cm bare. Arrange the apples on top, fold the edge over, brush the pastry with cream and sprinkle with the sesame seeds and remaining 10 g sugar.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: 40-50 min on the low shelf, turning once, until deep golden and the apples are tender. Cool 20 min before slicing. The low shelf helps the base crisp.

tips: Stir the tahini well before measuring; the oil separates in the jar.
The sesame spread keeps for 5 days in the fridge; let it soften before using.
Slice the apples about 3 mm thick so they soften in time.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for up to 2 days.
